correctness.rationale: For every finite generator, choose uniformization P=I+Q/lambda; diagonal R_s=(1-z)/(1-F_i(z)). First return gives inverse diagonal a_i/(1-z)+sum_{n>=1} f_{i,n}(1+...+z^{n-1}), strictly increasing for each nonabsorbing state, including transient/no-return mass. This proves continuous strict decrease from 1 to stationary mass (closed class) or 0 (transient), hence a unique threshold for each state below 1/2 and one global positivity interval. Cayley C=2R-I and nonnegative stochastic resolvent reduce all entrywise signs to these diagonals. Unconditional classification and directed-cycle identity follow exactly. Standalone script passed 5754 exact arithmetic checks for representative and random rational generators. Finite tests supplement, not substitute for, infinite/continuous proof.

originality.rationale: The strongest inspected identical-integrator prior establishes an exact diagonal-resolvent test for general generators and a monotone step cutoff only under reversibility; it expressly leaves nonreversible later positivity windows unclassified. The present proof proves strict diagonal resolvent monotonicity using a first-return generating function for every finite chain, so all generators have one sharp positivity window. Source comparisons with general RK positivity and Cayley M-matrix theory show those do not directly supply the claimed nonreversible crossing law. The reducible class and directed-three-cycle formula are consequences, not separate novel algorithms. The main remaining risk is an unlocated implication-equivalent Markov renewal result.
residual_risks: Classical first-return renewal formulas may have been applied to exact Crank–Nicolson Markov positivity already under alternate stochastic Cayley terminology; broad web/semantic searches do not certify priority.
The 1998 general RK positivity paper was accessed only as an abstract; no whole-document NOT_COVERING claim is based on it.
The inspected arXiv paper had targeted full-text sections read, not all sections; an uninspected appendix or obscure historical reference remains possible.
The result does not claim novelty for the Cayley identity, reversible threshold, standard first-return identity, or reducible stationary-class elementary facts.

value.rationale: A nonreversible finite generator can have complex eigenvalues, invalidating the positive real spectral mixture used by earlier exact Crank–Nicolson threshold analysis. The universal no-reentrance result closes that structural gap for all directed and reducible continuous-time Markov chains; it gives an exact numerical step-selection characterization and shows the only unconditionally safe chain classes. The directed three-cycle has the nontrivial sharp boundary 1+sqrt(5), strictly beyond the standard 2/lambda_max sufficient condition. This is a motivated qualitative integrator-stability boundary, not a mere arithmetic substitution or software reproduction.
